title: Partner-facing status brief and technical addendum for routing regression
content:
Executive summary (for partner ops):

Incident: IN-2025-422 — Intermittent model routing regression causing increased latency and sporadic degraded output for affected sessions
Impact window: 2025-11-29T22:12:00Z to 2025-11-29T23:41:00Z (peak 22:30–23:05 UTC)
Affected customers: Select Dedicated and Private deployments using regional pool us-west1 and customers relying on Smart Routing for multi-variant fallbacks
User-visible symptoms: transient 200–500ms additional tail latency on token responses for a subset of requests; in ~3% of requests routed to a quantized fallback variant, we observed minor coherence regressions (short, repeated phrases)

Customer-facing status page blurb (short):
We experienced a routing regression on 2025-11-29 that intermittently increased latency for some requests and caused a small number of responses to fall back to a quantized model variant with slightly lower output fidelity. The issue has been mitigated and normal service resumed at 2025-11-29T23:41:00Z UTC. If you continue to see degraded responses, please contact support with your request IDs.

Longer customer-facing update (use on status page with context):
What happened — brief: An autoscaler-induced state mismatch caused some routing entries to direct live traffic to an older, quantized model variant intended only for emergency fallback. This resulted in increased token latency and rare instances of slightly reduced response quality. No user data was exposed.
What we did: Engineering detected the mismatch via routing telemetry and rolled back the routing table to the validated snapshot. We also applied a hotfix to the autoscaler decision path to prevent stale entries.
Status: Resolved 2025-11-29T23:41:00Z UTC.

Technical appendix (concise, for partner SREs):
Root cause (short): A race condition between the Dedicated autoscaler shrink path and the Smart Routing table update produced stale routing entries that referenced a retired pool. The routing fallback logic accepted the retired entry and matched it to an available standby variant (a quantized model) without updating KV cache affinity, thereby serving traffic from an unintended variant.
Why this affected quality: The quantized fallback was functionally compatible but had been tuned for throughput, not fidelity, resulting in subtle repetitions and occasional truncation under the same prompt patterns.
Telemetry signals that triggered detection:
- spike in route mismatch metrics: route_table_mismatch_count +320% (22:28–22:34 UTC)
- tail latency increase for token emission: p99 rose from 180ms to 720ms for affected pool
- small uptick in automated quality monitors: eval_regression_score +0.07 on the rollout prompt set

Customer impact breakdown (estimate):
- Hosted (unaffected): 0 customers impacted (routing isolation maintained)
- Dedicated regional pool us-west1: ~7 paid customers experienced degraded tail latency and <0.1% saw quality regression
- Private (customer-managed VPCs with Redwood control plane enabled): 4 customers had transient routing to fallback variant; all preserved request logs and KV cache state; no data exfiltration

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Reverted routing table to last validated snapshot (22:38 UTC)
2) Applied a hotfix to autoscaler shrink path to block updates while route propagation is in flight (22:50 UTC)
3) Purged stale standby entries and forced revalidation of KV cache affinities for affected pools (23:01 UTC)
4) Notified impacted customers via direct channel and provided example request IDs for triage (23:10 UTC)

Recommended actions for customers (partner ops guidance):
- If you run on Dedicated: consider pinning critical routes to specific model versions (route.pin: true) until we deliver a permanent fix. This is a short CLI/Console toggle and will prevent automatic fallback selection for sensitive flows.
- If you run on Private with control plane enabled: confirm your control plane agent is at version >= 2025-11-20 (contains routing validation hooks). If not, schedule the agent update; our patch reduces the window for stale entries.
- For customers seeing persistent quality issues: share example request IDs and the approximate timestamps with support; our logs include the routed-variant field to accelerate investigation.

Template: customer outreach (direct message to impacted partner):
Subject: Incident IN-2025-422 — brief impact & next steps
Hi <PartnerOps>,
On 2025-11-29 we detected a routing regression affecting your Dedicated pool in us-west1. Impact: intermittent latency increases and a small number of responses routed to a throughput-optimized quantized fallback. We have rolled back the routing table and applied a hotfix; normal service resumed at 23:41 UTC.
Actions we took: reverted routing table, applied autoscaler guard, forced KV cache revalidation.
Actions you can take: pin critical routes and confirm control plane agent version.
We will follow up with a technical postmortem and a timeline of code changes. If you need immediate assistance, reply with request IDs or open a priority support ticket.

Postmortem summary draft (customer-facing):
Overview: On 2025-11-29, a sequence of autoscaler events led to a routing table mismatch that briefly directed traffic to an emergency fallback model variant. The fallback preserved availability but had different performance and fidelity characteristics.
Duration: ~1h29m from first anomaly to final verification.
Root cause: race condition between autoscaler shrink and routing propagation.
Impact: limited to specific Dedicated and Private customers; severity low-medium because availability was preserved.
Corrective actions: hotfix merged (MR 1893), expanded routing test coverage (integration tests added), new deployment gating to validate route propagation before pool shrink, and an operational playbook for accelerated rollback.
Preventive work planned:
- permanent autoscaler fix to serialize shrink operations with route propagation
- expanded canaries for routing updates across traffic slices
- dashboarding improvements: route_table_mismatch alert will be promoted from P3 -> P1 for early paging
Owner for fixes: infra-autoscaler team, expected delivery Q1 2026
Operational notes for CS/SE (how we talk to partners):
- Use the short blurb for status page.
- For high-touch partners, include the template outreach and offer a 1:1 walk-through of their affected requests.
- For partners on Dedicated contracts, propose a follow-up onboarding to pin critical routes and review fallback model choices.

Appendix: sample status page timeline entries (ready to paste)
Initial detection (22:30 UTC): Investigating elevated tail latency in us-west1 affecting a subset of Dedicated customers.
Mitigation in progress (22:45 UTC): Rolling back routing table snapshot and applying autoscaler guard to prevent stale updates.
Service restored (23:41 UTC): Normal routing and model behavior observed; monitoring.
Contact and escalation:
Customer success point: Marisol Gutierrez (marisol@redwood.ai)
Engineering lead: Ethan Cole (ethan@redwood.ai)
Priority support channel: #incidents-ops / Pager on-call
